 Oral Order

The instant revision is directed against the Judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge-IV, Patna City in Criminal Appeal No. 68 of 2023, convicting and sentencing the petitioner no. 1 to suffer simple imprisonment for two years and pay fine of Rs. 10,000/- and also convicting and sentencing the petitioner no. 2 to undergo simple imprisonment of three years and fine of Rs. 20,000/- for the offence under Section 498(A) of the I.P.C. with default clause of further imprisonment of six months for Patna High Court CR. REV.
No.529 of 2025(3) dt.09-07-2025 non payment of fine.

sentences.text: The petitioners were also intents to suffer imprisonment for two years and to pay fine of Rs. 10,000/- with default clause for the offence punishable under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Be it mentioned here that the court of appeal reverts the Judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate-I, Patna City in Complaint Case No. 1410 of 2015.

sentences.text: 3. I have heard the learned Senior counsel on behalf of the petitioners.
I have also perused the impugned Judgment.
4. The instant criminal revision is admitted.

5. Issue notice to opposite party no. 2 through ordinary process as well as under registered cover with A/D, requisites etc. for which must be filed within one week from the date of this order.
6.

The petitioners have also filed an application being I.A. No. 01 of 2025, praying for exemption from surrendering before the court of appeal to suffer sentence pending hearing of the instant revision on the ground that petitioner no. 1 is an old aged lady and petitioner no. 2 being the husband of opposite Patna High Court CR. REV. No.529 of 2025(3) dt.09-07-2025 party no. 2 is the sole bread earner of the family.
He also maintain his two children, aged about 16 and 17 years respectively.
He also pays maintenance allowance to the opposite party no. 2 @ Rs. 10,000/- per month.

If he is put in custody to suffer sentence, as passed by the court of appeal, scope of his earning would be seized and it would not be possible to pay maintenance allowance as well as to maintain the children, who are on the verge of their growing up and the old ailing mother.

7. Therefore, the petitioners have prayed for exemption of Rule 57(A) of the Rules of High Court at Patna which prescribe that in the case of revision under Sections 397 and 401 of the Cr.P.C (Section 438 and 442 of the B.N.S.S.), arising out of a conviction and sentence of imprisonment, the petition shall state whether the petitioner has surrendered or not.

If he has surrendered, petition shall be accompanied by a certified copy of the relevant order, if he has not surrendered, the petition shall be accompanied by an application seeking leave to surrender within the specified period, on sufficient cause being shown, the Bench may grant such time and on such condition as it thinks fit and proper,
directing the convict to surrender.
No revision shall be posted for admission unless the Patna High Court CR.
REV. No.529 of 2025(3) dt.09-07-2025 petitioner has surrendered to custody in the concerned court.
This Rule is pari materia to Rule 159 of the Jharkhand High Court Rule.

Rule 159 of Jharkhand High Court Rule was called upon to question in the case of Vivek Rai And Another Versus High Court of Jharkhand through Registrar General And Others, reported in (2015) 12 SCC 86.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court had the occasion to deal with the said provision contained in the Rules of Jharkhand High Court where the provision delineated in Section 482 of the Cr.P.C..

It was held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. vests inherent power of the High Court even to ignore the provision of Rule 159, in the instant case Rule 57(A) of the Rules of High Court at Patna in appropriate cases.

Paragraphs 9 and 10 of the aforesaid report are relevant and quoted below:-
"9.

It has not been disputed even by the learned counsel for the High Court that the Rule does not affect the inherent power of the High Court to exempt the requirement of surrender in exceptional situations.

It cannot thus, be argued that prohibition against posting of a revision petition for admission applies even to a situation where on an application of the Patna High Court CR. REV. No.529 of 2025(3)

2 dt.09-07-2025 petitioner, on a case being made out, the Court, in exercise of its inherent power, considers it appropriate to grant exemption from surrender having regard to the nature and circumstances of a case.

entities.text: Poonam Mehrotra vs The State Of Bihar on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the exception as found in corresponding Supreme Court Rules that if the Court grants exemption from surrender and directs listing of a case, the Rule cannot stand in the way of the Court's exercise of such jurisdiction, has to be assumed in the impugned Rule.
10. In these circumstances, we do not find any ground to hold that the impugned Rule suffers from any infirmity.
The writ petition is accordingly, dismissed."
9. Thus, it is clear from the Judgment of the Apex Court that in appropriate cases the High Court in exercise of inherent power may consider it appropriate to grant exemption from surrender.
10. In the instant case, it is the Judgment of reversal, which is under challenge.
The petitioners were aware about an order of acquittal by the Court of first instance.
Subsequently they were convicted.
It is not at all disputed that the petitioner no. 1 is presently aged about 67 years.
During the pendency of Patna High Court CR. REV. No.529 of 2025(3) dt.09-07-2025 the instant revision, arising out of a matrimonial dispute under Section 498A of the I.P.C.

, if the petitioner no. 1 is directed to surrender,
the revisional application filed by her would be infructuous.
Moreover, the petitioner no. 2 maintains his two children and mother.
He has been paying maintenance allowance to the opposite party no. 2 @ Rs. 10,000/- per month.

If he is taken to custody to suffer sentence, his source of income would be stopped and both the opposite party no. 2 and two grown up children of the parties would be compelled to live lives of destitute.
11. Considering such circumstances, I am inclined to allow the instant application.
I.A. No. 01 of 2025 is allowed.
12. The petitioners are exempted from surrendering before the court of appeal to suffer sentence till the disposal of the instant criminal revision.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J) pravinkumar/-
